text.arabic_uthmani: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقْطَعُوٓا۟ أَيْدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءًۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلًۭا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌۭ

baseline.text: Hırsızlık yapan erkeğin ve kadının, kazandıklarına karşılık Allah'tan caydırıcı bir ceza olarak ellerini kesin. Allah güçlüdür, doğru hüküm verendir.

findings.text: Haksız kazancın aracı olan elin kesilmesi, bu edinimi durduran ve başkalarını da alıkoyan toplumsal bir sınır oluşturur.

activation_trace.role: Physical separation supplies the concrete operation commanded by the imperative.
The bodily limb supplies the direct anatomical object of that operation.
Reciprocal return for an act makes the operation a consequence rather than an unmotivated injury.
Acquiring gain supplies the deed to which the consequence is attached.
A punishment that deters observers gives the bodily consequence a public preventive function.

changed_reading.after: The ayah presents a concrete bodily severance as an act-matched, publicly deterrent recompense for the male or female thief.
changed_reading.before: The ayah merely announces that theft receives punishment.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative to cut has the paired thieves' hands as its direct object, followed by recompense and deterrence clauses.
baseline_models.mechanism: Anatomical hands, physical severance, action-matched recompense, acquisition, and exemplary deterrence form a complete corporal-penal mechanism applying to both named genders.

activation_trace.role: Attribution of deeds to hands turns the named limb into the offender's operative instrument.
The image of earning limbs joins bodily instrument and acquisition in one lexical mechanism.
Corresponding return directs the acquired deed back toward its instrument.
Severance makes that instrumental correspondence materially visible.

changed_reading.after: The hand is selected as the acquiring and acting instrument, so the recompense visibly mirrors the channel of the deed.
changed_reading.before: The hand is an arbitrary body part selected for punishment.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Hands are named beside what the two offenders acquired.
baseline_models.mechanism: The hand is simultaneously the bodily target, the limb to which action is attributed, and an earning organ. The consequence therefore returns to the instrument through which acquisitive agency was exercised.

activation_trace.role: Inability to perform supplies a functional result of cutting beyond the material event itself.
Hand as power makes the object of interruption the offender's operative capacity.
The split-root image of reinforced power sharpens the capacity reading without replacing the bodily one.
A fetter that blocks movement supplies restraint as the intended social effect.

changed_reading.after: Cutting also carries the functional image of incapacitating the power by which another theft could be performed.
changed_reading.before: Cutting refers only to the removal of anatomy.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Cutting, hands, and deterrent restraint can each denote a loss or blocking of operative power.
baseline_models.mechanism: A hand can name power, cutting can produce inability, and deterrence can work as a restraining fetter. Alongside the corporal model, the construction can therefore foreground disabling the capacity to repeat the taking.

activation_trace.role: Secret slipping away supplies the covert transfer pattern of the offense.
Severing a connection turns the command into interruption of the relation enabling the taking.
Hand as possession identifies illicit control as the relation to be broken.
Restraining blockage supplies the continuing prevention after access is severed.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also images severing the offender's covert access to and control over what can be taken.
changed_reading.before: The command concerns only a body after a completed theft.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The thief, the cut, and the hands can be linked as covert withdrawal, severed connection, and possessed control.
baseline_models.mechanism: Theft moves something secretly into the taker's control. Cutting the hand can consequently image severing the covert channel of access and possession, while deterrent restraint prevents reconnection.

activation_trace.role: Hand as power anchors the changed reading in the focus object's operative capacity.
Extending and releasing a hand supplies the directional deployment of harmful reach.
Action attributed to the two opposed hands makes bodily reach answerable to the persons directing it.
Lethal harm supplies the endpoint accepted by one extended hand and refused by the other.

changed_reading.after: The focus hand is also the offender's outward reach, and the command interrupts agency capable of being extended toward harm.
changed_reading.before: The focus hand is a passive body part selected after the offense.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier scene twice joins a hand to extension toward another person and to killing, with the second speaker refusing the same reach. This makes the hand an enacted reach of agency and strengthens reading the focus command as interruption of a capacity deployed toward harm.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies extended hands, opposed intentions, and killing; I infer that the focus hand can denote actionable reach and that cutting blocks such reach. A live alternative is that 5:28 contributes only a literal hand scene with no functional implication for theft.
structural_cues: 5:28 repeats hand and extension in a balanced threat/refusal construction.
The narrative places controlled and uncontrolled bodily agency before the legal penalties.

activation_trace.role: The focus severance supplies the operation whose contextual configuration is being compared.
The repeated act-for-consequence frame places both rules in the same penal register.
The branch of plunder creates an acquisition overlap while the source construction names a wider offense class.
Departure from sound order supplies the broader social damage governing the more complex sanction.
Repeated physical separation confirms the concrete bodily possibility in the focus.
The explicitly paired bodily limb reinforces the anatomical reading of the focus object.
Feet added to hands supply the contextual escalation and distinguish the two configurations.
Taking unlike directions supplies the opposed-side arrangement that is absent from 5:38.

changed_reading.after: It is a specific corporal configuration within a sequence that differentiates offenses and the bodily scope of their sanctions.
changed_reading.before: The focus imperative is an isolated expression of punitive force.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby war-and-corruption rule repeats recompense, cutting, and hands but adds feet, opposite-side arrangement, and alternative sanctions. The repetition confirms a bodily-juridical register while the changed configuration locates 5:38 within differentiated responses rather than undirected severity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated legal vocabulary with different offenses, limbs, and alternatives; I infer calibrated differentiation between sanction configurations. A live alternative is that the two formulas are independent rules and should not be arranged on a single scale.
structural_cues: 5:33 offers killing, crucifixion, crosswise hand-foot cutting, or expulsion as alternatives.
5:38 repeats the recompense-plus-cutting pattern but names only the thieves and their hands.

activation_trace.role: The focus punishment supplies the deterrent boundary whose finality the surrounding repair language revises.
Capacity to overpower supplies a temporal enforcement threshold for the preceding sanction.
Repair opposed to corruption makes changed conduct, not verbal regret alone, the forward movement.
Covering the wrong and protecting its doer from its effect supplies a nonterminal horizon after wrongdoing.
Merciful tenderness prevents deterrent force from exhausting the sequence's account of the offender.

changed_reading.after: The sanction marks a serious boundary, but the adjacent sequence leaves the person capable of repair, forgiven standing, and renewed conduct.
changed_reading.before: The thief label and deterrent consequence define a terminal status.

context_deltas.mechanism: A pre-capture threshold appears for the preceding offense, and the ayah immediately after 5:38 joins post-wrongdoing return to active repair, protection from the sin's effect, and mercy. Deterrent restraint is therefore set inside a temporal arc that still admits restored conduct and standing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies temporal thresholds, post-wrongdoing repair, forgiveness, and mercy; I infer that the offender is not fixed permanently in the thief label. Because 5:34 concerns the preceding offense and 5:39 does not state a procedural consequence, a live alternative is that repentance changes divine standing without canceling the focus sanction.
structural_cues: Repentance occurs on both sides of 5:38, before capture in 5:34 and after wrongdoing with repair in 5:39.
5:39 immediately follows the focus and repeats divine acceptance, forgiveness, and mercy.

activation_trace.role: Attributing theft to a person exposes the epistemic step hidden inside the definite offender labels.
Falsehood supplies the danger of basing a severe judgment on corrupted reports.
Deflection from the proper direction supplies the mechanism of moving legal words away from their place.
Repeated judgment between people supplies the institutional act through which the rule is applied.
Equity supplies the required orientation of that judgment.
Testimony grounded in knowledge supplies an evidentiary counterweight to hearsay and distortion.
Inclination of desire supplies the pressure that can bend application away from the stated rule.
Absence of knowledge supplies the rejected alternative to informed divine judgment.

changed_reading.after: The male or female thief is a status to be truthfully established and equitably judged, insulated from hearsay, distortion, desire, and uninformed force.
changed_reading.before: Anyone called a thief is immediately exposed to the imperative.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus root includes attributing theft to a person. The later legal sequence warns of false hearing, displacement of words, desire-driven selection, and ignorant judgment, while repeatedly requiring judgment, equity, and knowledgeable witness. The thief designation thus reads as an adjudicated status, not a self-executing allegation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an attribution branch for thief and a sustained anti-distortion judgment sequence; I infer that the imperative presupposes verified classification and just adjudication. A live alternative is that the definite participles merely name the legal category while leaving evidentiary procedure unstated.
structural_cues: 5:41-50 forms a sustained judgment sequence around lies, textual displacement, witnesses, equity, desire, and informed judgment.
The focus closes with the same root that the context repeatedly uses for judging between people.

activation_trace.role: Act-matched return anchors proportional correspondence in the focus.
Concrete severance keeps bodily consequence present within the proportional model.
Bodily wounding supplies the material domain explicitly governed by correspondence.
Matching the consequence to the injury supplies a limit on punitive excess.
Relinquishing a material right as charity introduces a distinct nonretaliatory possibility in the legal field.
Judgment between people keeps proportionality within adjudication rather than private vengeance.

changed_reading.after: Recompense is read within a legal field of measured bodily correspondence and adjudicated limits, with waiver present nearby but not proven applicable to theft.
changed_reading.before: Recompense authorizes an unspecified degree of punitive severity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later rule enumerates body part against body part, places wounds under matched retaliation, allows relinquishment as charity, and returns to judgment. It sharpens focus recompense as bounded correspondence rather than open-ended vengeance while keeping bodily consequence live.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact bodily pairings, matched retaliation, relinquishment, and judgment; I infer a legal preference for bounded correspondence that sharpens the focus recompense. A live alternative is that neither the matching formula nor its waiver mechanism transfers procedurally from wounds to theft.
structural_cues: 5:45 lists life and four body parts in exact paired constructions before wounds and retaliation.
The same ayah places charitable relinquishment beside the matched bodily rule and closes with judgment.

remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not decide whether functional incapacitation is an additional image of literal severance or a genuinely alternative implementation.
The legal effect of repentance after 5:38 is not specified, and the pre-capture exception in 5:34 belongs to a different offense.
The nearby waiver rule establishes a legal possibility but does not state that it applies to theft.
The secret-listening, ripe-cut, and earning-wound models are visibly anchored but remain branch-distant resonances rather than settled legal readings.
strongest_changes: The extended-hand scene and the repeated hand-cutting rule make the hand both literal anatomy and enacted harmful reach.
The war-and-corruption sanction differentiates bodily configurations, so 5:38 reads as a calibrated legal case rather than free punitive force.
Immediate repair language prevents the thief label from becoming a permanent identity, while leaving the worldly effect of repentance unresolved.
The sustained lies, distortion, testimony, equity, and judgment sequence makes verified adjudication a necessary contextual layer.
The bodily-retaliation rule sharpens recompense as bounded correspondence and intensifies the hand-as-earning-instrument mirror.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly recombines hand, cutting, acquisition, recompense, restraint, and judgment across narrative and legal registers. That supports a strong corporal reading while preserving distinct functional, relational, and lexical activations instead of collapsing them into one interpretation.

activation_trace.role: Covert listening opens an auditory form of taking within the focus root.
Hearing that becomes uptake and compliance supplies the channel through which corrupt speech gains force.
Falsehood marks the received material as corrupt rather than neutral information.
Directional deflection supplies the manipulation performed after illicit uptake.
Meaning-bearing words supply the object being received, moved, and selectively deployed.

changed_reading.after: As a contained resonance, it also exposes covert appropriation of legal speech and the disabling of channels that turn distorted words into action.
changed_reading.before: The theft vocabulary activates only covert taking of material property.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries theft from property into illicit reception and manipulation of speech. It remains anchored in the focus thief root's secret-listening branch and in the later repeated hearing, falsehood, and displaced-word sequence. Downstream prose should present it only as a contextual lexical resonance, not as a replacement offense definition or a basis for transferring the corporal rule.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The thief root in 5:38 contains a secret-listening branch, while cutting and hands can denote severed connection and operative power.

activation_trace.role: The secondary image of cutting makes the consequence materially echo the imperative.
Harvest at ripeness supplies a temporal image in which an acquisition matures into its consequence.
The explicit severance gives the secondary recompense image a visible focus anchor.
Acquired gain supplies what figuratively ripens and is harvested back as consequence.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, recompense also sounds materially like a ripe cutting: what was acquired matures into the cut returned for it.
changed_reading.before: Recompense is an abstract label placed after the command.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's secondary mapping of the recompense root to cutting and harvest. It remains valid as a focus-only material echo joining recompense, acquisition, and the explicit cut. Downstream prose should call it wordplay-like reinforcement, never a lexical substitution for the ordinary recompense branch.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus places recompense between cutting and what was acquired, and its split mapped root contains cutting and harvest-at-maturity branches.

activation_trace.role: Deeds attributed to hands establish the focus limb as an accountable instrument.
Earning limbs fuse acquisition and bodily instrument inside the focus wording.
Bodily injury supplies the material consequence side of the cross-link.
Acquiring an action connects the later wound vocabulary back to what the focus offenders earned.
Hunting limbs repeat the image of a body part functioning as an acquiring agent.
Matched consequence binds bodily result back to the action performed by the acquiring limb.

changed_reading.after: The packet lets them form one material circuit: an acquiring limb performs the deed, and matched bodily consequence returns to that operative limb.
changed_reading.before: The hand, the earning, and the wound-like consequence are separate legal details.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-links the focus earning-limb branch with the later wound root's earning and hunting-limb branches, so it is more lexical than procedural. It remains anchored in hands, what they earned, and the packet's adjacent bodily-retaliation vocabulary. Downstream prose should use it to illuminate instrument-consequence mirroring, not to claim that 5:45 directly legislates 5:38.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins hands to earning, and the later wounds root joins bodily injury, earned action, and hunting limbs.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Illicit acquisition is answered by disabling its instrument.** `ك س ب B001` is seeking/obtaining benefit, `ق ط ع B001` severing, and `ن ك ل B001` a restraining shackle/check. Hand, gain, severance, and deterrence form an instrumental sequence. I infer that the penalty publicly interrupts the capacity by which stealthy acquisition was converted into possession.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The taking organ is severed to produce a social check.** Fixed **ق ط ع / B001** (“cutting off and severing”) targets the hands through which the acquisition occurred, while fixed **ن ك ل / B001** (“the restraining shackle or check”) and **B003** (“an exemplary deterrent punishment”) state the forward social role. The window places this after the mobility penalties of 5:33 and before repair in 5:39. I infer that bodily interruption is meant both to answer completed gain and to restrain repetition beyond the pair. The sentence reads as a backward-looking equivalence joined to a prospective deterrent mechanism.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:39’s immediate pairing of return with repair confirmed that deterrence aims beyond the severed act toward restoration of sound conduct.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector opening a fresh legal ruling while preserving adjacency to the prior punishment scene
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens 5:38 as controlled resumption. It keeps the ayah adjacent to 5:37, but it starts a fresh legal topic rather than extending the fire scene syntactically. Its compact joined delivery lets the ruling begin without a heavy break while still marking a register shift from eschatological description to prescriptive law.

topics.headline: fresh legal frame after 5:37
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:38 is adjacent to 5:37 but begins a new legal frame.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the opening connector as resumptive rather than simple coordination.

topics.headline: continuity with separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the connector carrying both sequence and boundary, so the two scenes stay adjacent without collapsing into one.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows treat the connector as preserving adjacency while maintaining a new legal unit.

topics.headline: compact audible launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ruling launch as a joined phrase rather than as a detached marker.
topics.reason: The bound particle joins to the following word in recitation, supporting a compact opening effect.

topics.headline: shift into legal address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the move from narrated punishment to a theft statute before the imperative appears.
topics.reason: Transition and boundary rows explicitly describe the discourse shift from 5:37 into 5:38.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine active participle naming a generic legal class before the consequent command
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّارِقُ}} ({{tr:al-sāriqu}}) is the first named legal class, a nominative active participle placed before the command as the topic to which {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) responds. The root pressure is not generic acquisition: the supplied theft field points to covert taking from protected possession. Variant rows sharpen the local choice, because the canonical singular active participle is broader than intensive, plural, or accusative alternatives. Echoes with Surah 12 theft-claim scenes (12:70; 12:73; 12:77; 12:81) contrast accusation language with this formal legal categorization.
words.root_gloss_range: stealthy taking and covert appropriation from protected possession; locally a legal offender label rather than every accusation scene

topics.headline: fronted generic offender class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ruling begin with classification before execution.
topics.reason: The word is a definite nominative active participle functioning as the opening topic.

topics.headline: covert protected-possession theft
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offender label evokes secret taking from protected possession, not taking in the abstract.
topics.reason: The supplied root evidence coherently narrows the theft image without contradicting the local participle.

topics.headline: canonical participle against variants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the canonical form names a legal class without adopting intensive, plural, or accusative variant parses.
topics.reason: Variant evidence is useful as contrast, but local QAC grammar keeps the canonical nominative active participle primary.

topics.headline: rare theft field in legal use
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish this legal use from theft-language clusters of claim, denial, and pledge elsewhere (12:70; 12:73; 12:77; 12:81; 60:12).
topics.reason: The recurrence rows provide concrete references but do not override the local legal syntax.

topics.headline: classification before command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s order: legal category first, imperative second.
topics.reason: Transition rows and clause evidence make the participle part of a topic-comment legal frame.

words.gloss_range: coordinating connector joining masculine and feminine thief labels as equal legal subjects
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) between the two thief labels is coordination, not loose addition. It makes {{ar:ٱلسَّارِقُ}} ({{tr:al-sāriqu}}) and {{ar:ٱلسَّارِقَةُ}} ({{tr:al-sāriqatu}}) one parallel legal pair before the command arrives. The repeated root and fused recitation make the gender pairing audible as a tight construction.

topics.headline: equal male-female coordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the feminine label is not an afterthought; both thief classes receive equal syntactic standing.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses the conjoined relation between the two thief nouns.

topics.headline: joining plus equalizing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the small connector carrying both addition and parity.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL semantic row identifies the conjunction as joining and equalizing the legal subjects.

topics.headline: bound link into second label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second label arrive as a compact continuation of the paired phrase.
topics.reason: The connector is a bound proclitic that fuses into the following assimilated form.

topics.headline: root reprise across the connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the theft root repeated across the conjunction as one legal pair.
topics.reason: The echo row explicitly ties the repeated root to the coordinated construction.

topics.headline: gender-paired legal refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the pair complete before the command applies.
topics.reason: Transition rows describe the conjunction creating the male-female legal pairing.

words.gloss_range: definite feminine active participle conjoined as the second member of the legal topic pair
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّارِقَةُ}} ({{tr:al-sāriqatu}}) completes the fronted legal pair as a nominative feminine active participle, not as a subordinate add-on. It also supplies the second member needed for later dual forms in {{ar:أَيْدِيَهُمَا}} ({{tr:aydiyahumā}}) and {{ar:كَسَبَا}} ({{tr:kasabā}}). The same covert-taking root image is explicitly feminized here, while variant rows and the pledge echo (60:12) remain contrastive evidence rather than replacements for the canonical singular topic form.
words.root_gloss_range: same theft-root field as the masculine label, locally recast in explicit feminine active-participle form

topics.headline: explicit feminine legal topic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees explicit feminine inclusion inside the legal subject, not a masculine class silently extended later.
topics.reason: The word is a nominative active participle conjoined to the masculine topic with equal syntactic standing.

topics.headline: theft image explicitly feminized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same covert theft-root field applied in a distinct feminine form.
topics.reason: The root evidence belongs to the same s-r-q field while the local form marks feminine participation.

topics.headline: canonical feminine singular against variants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader compares the canonical feminine singular with plural, intensive, and accusative alternatives while keeping the local parse primary.
topics.reason: Variant evidence clarifies the form choice, but QAC grammar keeps the nominative feminine active participle local.

topics.headline: rare feminine theft form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this explicit feminine theft form against the wider theft field and the women’s pledge context (60:12).
topics.reason: The echo rows give concrete distributional and cross-surah provenance.

topics.headline: topic pair completed before command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this second noun completes the pair that later dual morphology will reference.
topics.reason: The feminine topic supplies the second antecedent for the dual possessor and dual verb later in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: apodotic particle turning the thief-topic pair into a consequent legal command
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge that converts the named thief pair into a legal response. It scopes over both opening subjects and runs directly into {{ar:ٱقْطَعُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:iqṭaʿū}}), so the command is not free-floating punishment but the answer to the classified case. The fāʾ-plus-imperative pattern also aligns the verse with the legal sentencing construction in 24:2.

topics.headline: topic becomes consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact pivot from offender classification to executable ruling.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle as apodotic, with scope over the preceding legal topic.

topics.headline: sequence plus legal dependence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the particle is more than then; it makes the command depend on the thief topic.
topics.reason: The semantic row preserves immediate linkage, consequence, and apodotic response together.

topics.headline: fused into the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears cause and command as one compact pronounced unit.
topics.reason: The particle is directly bound to the following imperative in the surface form.

topics.headline: sentencing formula parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the construction to another named-offender-plus-command legal formula (24:2).
topics.reason: The supplied parallel is concrete and constructional, so it survives as formula provenance.

topics.headline: class-to-command pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from legal subject to prescribed act without a separate conditional particle.
topics.reason: Transition rows identify the particle as the hinge from noun pair to imperative.

words.gloss_range: Form I plural imperative commanding the legal addressees to cut or sever the specified object
words.prose: {{ar:ٱقْطَعُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:iqṭaʿū}}) changes the ayah from third-person offender labels to a second-person plural legal addressee. It governs {{ar:أَيْدِيَهُمَا}} ({{tr:aydiyahumā}}) as its object and functions as the response to the fronted thief pair. The q-ṭ-ʿ field gives real severance and decisive-settlement pressure, but local grammar keeps physical cutting as the active sense. Same-surah contrast with the intensified Form II cutting in 5:33 narrows the local form: this is the direct Form I theft command, not the broader ḥirābah penalty.
words.root_gloss_range: cutting, severing, interruption, traversal, and decisive settlement; locally physical severance in an imperative legal command

topics.headline: plural imperative governs object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices agency shift from the two offenders to an addressed legal authority or community.
topics.reason: The verb is a 2mp imperative with no separate overt subject and a forced direct object.

topics.headline: severance with legal finality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears physical severance as the local action while also noticing the root’s legal finality pressure.
topics.reason: The broader q-ṭ-ʿ field includes decisive settlement, but the direct object and imperative select concrete cutting.

topics.headline: Form I and object contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a simpler Form I theft command against intensified or object-shifted alternatives.
topics.reason: Variant and form rows are contrastive; they do not replace the canonical Form I imperative governing hands.

topics.headline: contrast with 5:33 cutting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare 5:38 with 5:33 and see a narrower theft penalty form.
topics.reason: The same-surah contrast is explicit and useful, but it grades the local command rather than importing 5:33’s scope.

topics.headline: command-object-rationale pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command as the structural pivot between legal class, hand object, and rationale.
topics.reason: The command sits after the apodotic particle and governs the object and purpose specifications.

words.gloss_range: plural hand noun as the direct object, carrying a dual possessor suffix that points back to the male-female thief pair
words.prose: {{ar:أَيْدِيَهُمَا}} ({{tr:aydiyahumā}}) is the direct object of the cutting command, but its form is marked: a plural hand noun with a dual possessor suffix. That construction binds the object to both thief labels while leaving distributive scope live. The hand root’s agency range survives because hands are means of action, but the local object role keeps bodily hands primary. Variant evidence about right hands or oaths narrows rather than replaces the canonical object, and echoes such as 36:65 connect hands with earned accountability.
words.root_gloss_range: hand, power, possession, means, favor, and agency; locally bodily hands as object, with agency imagery retained but narrowed by syntax

topics.headline: plural hands with dual possessor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the unusual number layering: plural hands belong to the two-person offender pair.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as object with dual suffix, and CRITICAL rows make distributive scope explicit.

topics.headline: bodily hand plus agency range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the object is not random: the hand carries agency and capacity imagery while remaining a bodily object here.
topics.reason: The lexical range includes power and means, but the imperative governs this word as a concrete direct object.

topics.headline: right-hand or oath variant contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that right-hand restriction is not explicit in the canonical surface, even though variant evidence makes that narrowing visible.
topics.reason: The bundle notes possible narrowing, but the local surface names hands without an explicit right-hand word.

topics.headline: hands and earned accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the cut hands to accountability motifs where hands and earned deeds meet (36:65; 5:11; 5:28; 5:33).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide concrete references and support recurrence without changing the local object role.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative purpose noun naming the cutting as recompense tied to the earned cause
words.prose: {{ar:جَزَآءًۢ}} ({{tr:jazāʾan}}) begins the rationale after the command-object unit. As an indefinite accusative purpose noun, it frames the cutting as recompense, and {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}) then supplies the earned cause. The j-z-y field is broader than punishment alone, including proportional return and sufficiency, so the local penalty is presented as requital for what was acquired. It also pairs with {{ar:نَكَٰلًۭا}} ({{tr:nakālan}}): recompense looks backward to the deed, deterrence forward to prevention.
words.root_gloss_range: recompense, repayment, requital, sufficiency, reward, or punishment; locally negative legal recompense proportioned to what was earned

words.gloss_range: compound causal preposition plus relative pronoun: because of what they earned
words.prose: {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}) fuses cause and open reference. The bāʾ ties {{ar:جَزَآءًۢ}} ({{tr:jazāʾan}}) to the following earned action, while the relative mā leaves the object open until {{ar:كَسَبَا}} ({{tr:kasabā}}) completes it. This makes the rationale proportional to what the two acquired, not merely attached as a vague circumstance.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect dual verb naming the completed acquisition by the two offender referents
words.prose: {{ar:كَسَبَا}} ({{tr:kasabā}}) closes the relative clause begun by {{ar:بِمَا}} ({{tr:bimā}}). Its perfect dual ending routes the subject back to the male-female thief pair and presents the cause as completed two-person agency. The k-s-b root is morally broad earning or acquisition, so the local phrasing makes theft answerable as gain under accounting. Echoes with hand-and-earning scenes such as 36:65 reinforce that the hand object and the earned cause belong to the same accountability network.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative purpose noun naming deterrent warning as the second rationale
words.prose: {{ar:نَكَٰلًۭا}} ({{tr:nakālan}}) adds the second purpose of the penalty. Where {{ar:جَزَآءًۢ}} ({{tr:jazāʾan}}) answers the completed act, {{ar:نَكَٰلًۭا}} ({{tr:nakālan}}) projects the consequence outward as deterrence. The n-k-l field makes that deterrence concrete: recoil, restraint, and exemplary warning are all in play. Its recurrence with the Sabbath-breaker warning (2:66) shows a communal deterrent pattern, while the local syntax keeps it tied to the theft ruling.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine proper name governed by the source preposition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is the governed source term after {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}), so the rationale closes by naming God as the origin rather than leaving deterrence as human policy. The broader divine-name field adds worship and ultimate authority, but the local case keeps the role genitive source. The near repetition with later {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is central: the name moves from source phrase to nominative subject of the attribute seal. Legal parallels such as 5:33 and 5:95 show the same divine authority field around punishment and recompense.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine proper name as subject of the final two-predicate nominal sentence
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) repeats the divine name instead of using a pronoun, and the case shift matters: after genitive {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}), this nominative form becomes the subject of {{ar:عَزِيزٌ}} ({{tr:ʿazīzun}}) and {{ar:حَكِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:ḥakīmun}}). Formula rows show the phrase entering a recurrent divine-attribute seal, while the next ayah contrasts this penalty closure with repentance, forgiveness, and mercy (5:39).

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative first predicate asserting divine might in the closing nominal sentence
words.prose: {{ar:عَزِيزٌ}} ({{tr:ʿazīzun}}) is the first predicate of {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), so might is asserted as a quality inside the closing sentence, not merely used as a title. The root field adds invincibility, inaccessibility, honor, and stable strength, fitting the legal closure. Yet the word does not stand alone: matching form, cadence, and co-occurrence bind it to {{ar:حَكِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:ḥakīmun}}), so the ruling is sealed by authority joined to wise judgment rather than by raw force alone. A penalty parallel in 5:95 and the boundary with 5:37 reinforce the authority field.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative second predicate completing the divine attribute closure
words.prose: {{ar:حَكِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:ḥakīmun}}) is the final predicate, sharing {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) as subject with {{ar:عَزِيزٌ}} ({{tr:ʿazīzun}}).
